saturation.reason: Wave 20 used the same frozen corpus v1 but a materially different class/lifecycle/municipal-role-first strategy. It produced zero new current actionable gaps within the frozen perimeter after mapping candidates back to the allowed oracle scopes and canonical evidence. Wave 19 and Wave 20 are therefore two consecutive independent clean sweeps on an unchanged corpus.

method.independenceFromWave19: Wave 19 started from source/programme directories. Wave 20 instead searched by benefit class, lifecycle and municipal role (grant, technical assistance, finance, asset transfer, award, cascade/FSTP, PCP/PPI, borrower/requester/required-beneficiary/partner), and only afterwards mapped surfaced candidates to the frozen oracle scopes and canonical corpus.
canonicalComparisonOrder: map candidate to a frozen oracle scope
verify concrete municipal role and operational benefit
known Waves 1-18 plus clean Wave 19 controls

outOfCorpusCandidatesForV2.note: The EIB has general public-sector/local-authority loan products with a documented project cycle, but frozen v1 includes the EIB only through the specifically enumerated eib-advisory scope (ELENA, ADAPT, C3, JASPERS, InvestEU Advisory Hub). Expanding that oracle scope to general EIB lending would require corpus v2 and is not allowed mid-gate.

gateConclusion.note: The audit freeze condition is satisfied. No engine/config/discovery implementation change is included in Wave 20; hardening should begin as a subsequent, explicitly tracked phase while PR #161 remains draft and unmerged until authorised.

waveConclusion: Wave 20 is the second consecutive independent clean sweep over the unchanged frozen corpus v1. The saturation gate is met at 2/2. The audit demonstrates a sufficiently saturated v1 corpus for discovery hardening to begin, without claiming that every conceivable future municipal opportunity family in Europe has been exhausted.
